mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising the cost of capital and depressing corporate earnings growth, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY compared to baseline periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than -0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month averages signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE and rising PAYEMS) above 63% for four consecutive months signals improved labor supply, which increases productive capacity and supports higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS rising for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when both UNRATE is stable and PAYEMS rises for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.5% for six consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings for retail and related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 0.5% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher when RSAFS increases by more than 0.5% for six consecutive months.
